title: Bag of Words, TF-IDF, and Text Representation

questions.question: What vocabulary indices does build_vocab assign to ["cat", "dog"] followed by ["dog", "fish"]?
options: The indices are randomized for every document
questions.explanation: build_vocab inserts unseen tokens in first-seen order and uses the current vocabulary size as the next index.

questions.question: For a vocabulary ["cat", "dog"], what row does bag_of_words produce for ["dog", "dog"]?
questions.explanation: The function counts occurrences at each vocabulary index, so dog contributes two to the second column.

questions.question: What does document_frequency count for one vocabulary term?
options: The number of documents whose count for the term is greater than zero
The total number of times the term appears in the whole corpus
The term's character length in each document
The number of vocabulary entries after normalization
questions.explanation: The loop increments df[j] once per row when count > 0, regardless of whether that row contains one or many occurrences.

questions.question: What IDF does inverse_document_frequency([3], n_docs=3) return?
questions.explanation: The smoothed formula is log((3+1)/(3+1))+1 = log(1)+1 = 1.

questions.question: How does tfidf compute term frequency before multiplying by IDF?
options: It replaces every nonzero count with one
It divides each count by the vocabulary size
It divides each count by the total token count in that document
It uses the raw count and ignores document length
questions.explanation: For each row, tf is c/sum(row), with an all-zero row handled as zeros before the IDF product.

questions.question: Why can cosine_similarity be implemented as a dot product after l2_normalize?
options: L2 normalization makes every vector one-hot
The dot product automatically counts shared words without weights
Cosine similarity is defined as the sum of raw token counts
Both vectors have unit length, so their dot product is cosine similarity
questions.explanation: The cosine denominator is the product of the norms; after each norm is one, only the dot product remains.
